title: Meilleurs ETF climat : guide d'investissement responsable
summary: Meilleurs ETF climat : comment les choisir selon les méthodologies PAB/CTB, les frais (TER) et l'éligibilité au PEA. Exemples et risque de perte en capital.
body_text: Mis à jour le 28 juillet 2026 Un ETF climat est un fonds indiciel qui investit dans des entreprises sélectionnées pour réduire l'empreinte carbone du portefeuille, souvent via les méthodologies PAB ou CTB alignées sur l'Accord de Paris. Ce guide compare les meilleurs ETF climat éligibles ou non au PEA et détaille les critères pour choisir selon son profil. L'essentiel Un ETF climat applique une méthodologie précise (PAB, CTB ou bas carbone) qui conditionne l'exclusion des énergies fossiles et la trajectoire de décarbonation. Les ETF PAB imposent au moins 50 % de réduction d'intensité carbone et une baisse de 7 % par an, contre 30 % pour les CTB. Les ETF thématiques « énergies propres » comme l'INRG sont bien plus volatils qu'un ETF climat diversifié type MSCI World. Le TER varie fortement : environ 0,15 % pour un PAB zone euro, jusqu'à 0,65 % pour un thématique clean energy. Seuls les ETF d'actions européennes sont éligibles au PEA ; les ETF mondiaux ou clean energy en sont exclus. Qu'est-ce qu'un ETF climat ? Un ETF climat est un panier d'actions choisies pour leur faible empreinte carbone ou leur rôle dans la transition énergétique, selon une méthodologie d'indice définie. Les meilleurs ETF climat ne sont pas seulement des instruments financiers. Ils sont des catalyseurs de changement, dirigeant des milliards de dollars vers les entreprises qui redéfinissent nos systèmes énergétiques et industriels. Comment fonctionne un ETF climat ? Un ETF climat est un panier d’actions sélectionnées pour leur impact positif sur l'environnement, plutôt que pour leur seule rentabilité. Ces ETF combinent performance financière et impact environnemental positif, offrant aux investisseurs une solution simple et efficace. Chaque ETF climat suit une méthodologie spécifique. Certains ciblent les entreprises leaders en décarbonation, d'autres excluent les grands pollueurs, et certains se concentrent sur les pionniers des énergies renouvelables. Pourquoi investir dans les meilleurs ETF climat ? L'investissement dans les ETF climat constitue une approche envisageable parmi d'autres. Les risques climatiques, qu'ils soient réglementaires, physiques ou réputationnels, redéfinissent les perspectives de succès en bourse. Les entreprises proactives dans la transition vers le bas-carbone ne se limitent pas à remplir des obligations RSE ; elles attirent des capitaux, des talents et évitent les sanctions. Investir dans les ETF climat peut être une option de gestion patrimoniale tenant compte de certaines tendances de marché. Cela permet également de concilier convictions personnelles et objectifs financiers. Différentes stratégies des ETF climat Les ETF climat adoptent diverses approches : Certains suivent strictement les indices alignés sur l’Accord de Paris (PAB), avec une réduction significative de l'empreinte carbone et l'exclusion des énergies fossiles. D'autres utilisent les indices CTB (Climate Transition Benchmark), favorisant une transition progressive sans exclure complètement les secteurs en mutation. Les ETF "faible carbone" privilégient les entreprises avec de faibles émissions. Des fonds thématiques se concentrent sur les énergies renouvelables , l'efficacité énergétique ou la mobilité propre. Cette variété de stratégies reflète les différentes perspectives sur la transition écologique. Chaque ETF fait un choix stratégique, influençant non seulement les marchés financiers mais aussi les politiques environnementales et sociales. Atteignez vos Objectifs Avec les Objectifs, fixez vos projets (matelas de sécurité, achat immobilier, retraite) et suivez votre avancée, calculée sur votre patrimoine réel. Créer votre objectif Comment choisir un ETF climat ? Choisir un ETF climat est comparable à sélectionner les ingrédients pour un plat qui doit être savoureux, sain et durable. Chaque option verte comporte des nuances, des compromis et parfois des pièges. Les investisseurs avertis ne se laissent pas séduire uniquement par le marketing. Ils examinent minutieusement les détails. La première question à se poser est : "Qu'est-ce qui se cache vraiment sous le capot ?". Les ETF climatiques utilisent des méthodologies d'indices très variées. Certains fonds se limitent à exclure le charbon, tandis que d'autres exigent une réduction annuelle des émissions de carbone. La différence entre un ETF "faible carbone" et un ETF "Paris-Aligned Benchmark" (PAB) est significative. Un investisseur exigeant va donc examiner plusieurs aspects : L'intensité carbone du portefeuille : Il s'agit de la quantité de CO₂ émise par million d'euros de chiffre d'affaires. Un chiffre bas indique une orientation vers la durabilité. La part d'entreprises "vertes" : Il est important de vérifier le pourcentage de revenus provenant d'activités durables, sachant que la définition de "vert" peut varier. L'alignement avec l'Accord de Paris : Les indices PAB et CTB exigent une réduction immédiate de l'empreinte carbone et une trajectoire de baisse annuelle. L'exclusion des énergies fossiles : Certains ETF excluent toute entreprise impliquée dans le charbon, le pétrole ou le gaz, tandis que d'autres excluent seulement les plus polluantes. Les critères financiers sont également cruciaux : Frais sur encours (TER) : Les coûts peuvent varier significativement, un TER compétitif se situe entre 0,15 % et 0,30 %. Encours sous gestion : Un fonds robuste dépasse souvent les 300 millions d'euros, évitant ainsi les risques de fermeture ou de problèmes de liquidité. Tracking error : Un écart de suivi élevé peut indiquer des difficultés à suivre l'indice de référence. Méthode de réplication : Il est essentiel de choisir entre une réplication physique, offrant plus de transparence, et une réplication synthétique , qui peut introduire un risque de contrepartie mais permet une diversification mondiale. Un aspect souvent sous-estimé est la composition réelle du portefeuille . Certains ETF "climat" peuvent être dominés par des géants de la tech ou de la finance, ce qui peut entraîner une concentration sectorielle inattendue. D'autres, axés sur les énergies renouvelables, peuvent être très volatils. Les ETF renouvelables sont souvent très volatils. Cette volatilité s'explique par plusieurs facteurs : Leur exposition à des petites capitalisations. Les fluctuations météorologiques qui influencent la production d'énergie. Leur forte sensibilité aux hausses des taux d'intérêt. La transparence est également vitale. Les meilleurs émetteurs fournissent des rapports détaillés sur leur méthodologie, composition et scores ESG. D'autres peuvent se limiter à des promesses vagues. Un investisseur diligent lira la documentation technique et comparera les indices. Vous hésitez encore entre gestion active et gestion passive pour choisir vos ETF climat ? Si le sujet vous paraît complexe ou que vous manquez de temps pour comparer, notre article détaillé « ETF gestion active ou passive : quelle est la meilleure ? » présente les caractéristiques des deux approches à titre informatif. Il suit un indice conforme à l'Accord de Paris, vise une réduction annuelle de 7 % des émissions de carbone et exclut les entreprises fortement polluantes. Il se concentre exclusivement sur la zone euro. Ce fonds porte l'ISIN LU2182388582 ; sa fiche complète est consultable sur JustETF . Avec un TER de seulement 0,15 %, cet ETF affiche des frais réduits. Il inclut des entreprises européennes leaders dans la transition énergétique, comme Schneider Electric et Iberdrola. La réplication physique permet une visibilité sur les actifs détenus. Cependant, cet ETF sacrifie la diversification géographique pour se concentrer sur l'Europe. Bien que l'Europe soit proactive en matière de réglementation climatique, elle représente seulement une partie de l'innovation mondiale dans ce domaine. De plus, la concentration sectorielle de cet ETF dans l'industrie, la finance et la technologie peut augmenter la volatilité en cas de chocs sectoriels. Les investisseurs doivent être conscients de ces aspects. Répartition par secteur Amundi MSCI EMU Climate Net Zero Ambition PAB UCITS ETF Acc (PABM) - Valeurs au 29 Juillet 2026 Amundi CAC 40 ESG UCITS ETF DR (C40) Le CAC 40 ESG représente l'approche française de l'investissement responsable. Ce fonds choisit des entreprises françaises de premier plan selon des critères ESG stricts, tout en évitant les secteurs controversés. Il inclut des secteurs tels que le luxe, l'industrie et la santé, et met en avant une forte présence nationale. Ce fonds porte l'ISIN LU1681046931 ; sa fiche complète est consultable sur JustETF . Ce fonds attire ceux qui cherchent à combiner un engagement environnemental avec le soutien à l'économie française. Avec un TER de 0,25 %, il reste abordable pour un ETF ESG. La réplication physique assure également une grande transparence. Cependant, il présente une double concentration : sectorielle (industrie, luxe) et géographique (presque exclusivement en France). Ce fonds, qui suit l’indice S&P Global Clean Energy, regroupe des entreprises mondiales actives dans la production ou la technologie des énergies renouvelables. Il porte l'ISIN IE00B1XNHC34 et affiche un encours d'environ 2,77 Md€ ; sa fiche complète est consultable sur JustETF . Le fonds répartit ses positions entre les utilities (environ 41 %), l'industrie (environ 32 %) et la technologie (environ 24 %) , avec des acteurs de la production et de l'équipement en énergie propre. Ses principales lignes incluent Bloom Energy, First Solar, Enphase Energy et China Yangtze Power (composition au 28/07/2026, source JustETF). Répartition par secteur iShares Global Clean Energy Transition UCITS ETF (INRG) - Valeurs au 29 Juillet 2026 Le fonds ne se limite pas à suivre la tendance verte. Il applique des filtres ESG et exclut les entreprises avec des émissions carbone élevées. Cependant, la volatilité de l’INRG montre que la transition énergétique est complexe, influencée par les cycles d’investissement, les politiques publiques et la concurrence technologique. Attention au TER de 0,65 %, qui est supérieur à la moyenne des ETF larges et affecte la performance à long terme. L’INRG est également un exemple en matière de diversification géographique. Avec des investissements principalement aux États-Unis, en Chine, au Brésil et en Israël, il offre une couverture mondiale mais le rend inéligible au PEA, le Plan d'Épargne en Actions. Après le boom vert de 2020-2021, l'énergie propre a corrigé brutalement tandis que le S&P 500 a progressé plus régulièrement, illustrant la volatilité d'un secteur thématique. Le graphique ci-dessus compare l’évolution de l’ETF iShares Global Clean Energy à celui de l’indice S&P 500. La courbe Clean Energy montre une spectaculaire envolée lors du "boom vert" de 2020-2021. Suivie d’une chute tout aussi brutale, illustrant sa grande volatilité. À l’inverse, la trajectoire du S&P 500 progresse de façon régulière. Cela montre bien la différence entre la stabilité d’un indice diversifié et le caractère cyclique d’un secteur thématique. Amundi MSCI World Climate Paris Aligned UCITS ETF Acc (PABW) Le PABW répond à la demande d’alignement avec l’Accord de Paris, mais à l’échelle mondiale. Ce fonds impose une réduction annuelle de 7 % de la trajectoire de décarbonation et une diminution de 50 % de l’intensité carbone par rapport à l’indice MSCI World classique. Il s’agit d’un des ETF les plus rigoureux en termes de méthodologie climatique. Selon le règlement délégué (UE) 2020/1818, un indice Paris-Aligned Benchmark doit réduire son intensité carbone d'au moins 50 % par rapport à son univers d'investissement et la diminuer de 7 % par an. Ce fonds porte l'ISIN IE000CL68Z69 , pour un TER de 0,20 % ; sa fiche complète est consultable sur JustETF . Malgré l’application de filtres climatiques, les grandes capitalisations technologiques américaines comme Apple, Microsoft et Nvidia dominent le fonds. Elles ont une faible intensité carbone relative et un poids significatif dans l’économie mondiale. Répartition par secteur Amundi MSCI World Climate Paris Aligned UCITS ETF Acc - Valeurs au 29 Juillet 2026 Comment investir dans les ETF climat sans se tromper ? Diversification et gestion des risques Il est tentant de se concentrer uniquement sur des investissements "propres" ou "bas carbone". Cependant, la volatilité des ETF thématiques, en particulier ceux axés sur les énergies renouvelables, montre que la transition écologique comporte des défis. Les cycles boursiers, les politiques publiques et les innovations technologiques peuvent rapidement changer la situation. Un portefeuille axé sur le climat gagne à conserver une diversification adéquate. Par exemple, les ETF climatiques européens tendent à être surpondérés dans les secteurs industriels ou financiers et se concentrent souvent sur une région spécifique. En revanche, les ETF mondiaux synthétiques offrent une diversification plus large, mais avec un alignement climatique potentiellement moins strict. Il est également crucial de surveiller le risque de contrepartie. Les ETF à réplication synthétique dépendent des swaps avec des banques. Bien que la réglementation UCITS offre certaines protections, le risque zéro n'existe pas. C'est un risque à surveiller attentivement. Importance de la recherche et de l’analyse Les détails sont cruciaux dans la finance durable. Un ETF étiqueté "climat" peut ne pas être aligné sur l'Accord de Paris, et un label ESG ne garantit pas une faible empreinte carbone. Les méthodologies des indices varient considérablement : Certains excluent simplement le charbon, D'autres exigent une réduction annuelle des émissions, D'autres se basent uniquement sur un score ESG global. Avant d'investir, il est essentiel d'examiner attentivement la composition du fonds. Identifiez les principales entreprises incluses, la proportion de revenus "verts" et si les entreprises sont en transition ou déjà exemplaires. Ces informations peuvent distinguer un investissement véritablement responsable d'un simple vernis écologique. Certaines entreprises françaises sont tenues de publier leur bilan des émissions de gaz à effet de serre ("bilan carbone"). Cet impact carbone est accessible en toute transparence pour le public et consultable sur le site de l’Ademe . La stabilité de l'encours est aussi à considérer. Un ETF gérant moins de 100 millions d'euros est plus susceptible de fermer, ce qui pourrait entraîner des ventes forcées et des coûts imprévus. Opter pour des fonds bien établis est aussi un investissement dans la durabilité. Choisir le meilleur ETF climat en fonction de son profil d’investisseur Il n'y a pas de "meilleur" ETF climat universel, mais des options adaptées à différents profils et convictions. Selon vos priorités : Un ETF PAB européen à réplication physique privilégie l'exigence climatique. Un ETF synthétique sur le MSCI World ou le S&P 500 ESG offre une diversification mondiale plus large. Les frais de gestion (TER) ont un impact sur la performance nette : sur dix ans, un écart de frais réduit le rendement final. La fiscalité est un paramètre à considérer. Vérifiez toujours l'éligibilité PEA de l'ETF pour optimiser la performance nette de votre investissement. Des applications comme Finary permettent de centraliser le suivi de ses ETF et de mesurer l'empreinte carbone comme les frais réels de son portefeuille, tous courtiers confondus. Quel ETF climat choisir pour commencer ? Il n'existe pas d'ETF climat universel : le bon choix dépend de votre priorité, exigence climatique maximale, diversification mondiale ou éligibilité au PEA. Comprendre la méthodologie de l'indice, remettre en question les labels et diversifier restent les meilleurs réflexes. Les ETF climat offrent une opportunité aux investisseurs. Ils peuvent conjuguer performance financière et engagement environnemental. Centralisez votre patrimoine PEA, livrets d'épargne, cryptomonnaies, actions, immobilier, comptes bancaires. Découvrir Finary Questions fréquentes Quelle est la différence entre un ETF PAB et un ETF CTB ? Un ETF PAB (Paris-Aligned Benchmark) impose une réduction d'au moins 50 % de l'intensité carbone par rapport à son univers d'investissement et exclut les énergies fossiles. Un ETF CTB (Climate Transition Benchmark) vise 30 % et reste investi dans des secteurs en transition. Les deux appliquent une décarbonation de 7 % par an. Un ETF climat est-il éligible au PEA ? Seuls les ETF composés d'actions européennes sont éligibles au PEA, comme l'Amundi MSCI EMU Climate PAB ou le CAC 40 ESG. Les ETF mondiaux, comme le MSCI World Climate Paris Aligned, ou thématiques, comme l'iShares Global Clean Energy, en sont exclus car ils investissent hors zone euro. Les ETF climat sont-ils plus risqués que les ETF classiques ? Cela dépend de leur composition. Un ETF climat large, aligné sur le MSCI World, présente un risque proche d'un ETF actions mondial. Les ETF thématiques « énergies propres » sont bien plus volatils, en raison de leur exposition aux petites capitalisations et de leur sensibilité aux taux d'intérêt. Comment repérer le greenwashing d'un ETF climat ? Il faut examiner la méthodologie de l'indice plutôt que le seul label. Un ETF « ESG » ne garantit pas une faible empreinte carbone. Vérifiez l'intensité carbone du portefeuille, la part de revenus verts, l'exclusion réelle des énergies fossiles et la transparence des rapports de l'émetteur. Quels frais attendre sur un ETF climat ? Le TER varie selon la stratégie : environ 0,15 % pour un ETF PAB zone euro comme l'Amundi PAB, 0,25 % pour un CAC 40 ESG, et jusqu'à 0,65 % pour un ETF thématique clean energy comme l'INRG. Sur dix ans, cet écart de frais réduit sensiblement la performance nette. title: Omnichannel Marketing: Third-Party Cookies vs First-Party Data
body_text: An omnichannel marketing strategy is a gold standard for effective brand messaging. By leveraging consumer data gleaned from third-party cookies, advertisers can get the right message to the right customer at the right time, regardless of channel or device. It's no wonder brands with robust omnichannel strategies increase average order value by 13% and purchase frequency by 250%. The coming cookieless future could threaten that success. Without third-party cookies, advertisers will struggle to track customers across channels and devices, analyze their journeys, and deliver personalized content and offers. It's easy to assume that cookie deprecation means the death of omnichannel marketing, but that's definitely not the case. If you have the right data, omnichannel marketing still holds the key to success. Key takeaways: Consistency in branding and messaging across every channel is among the key elements an omnichannel marketing strategy prioritizes. We can expect the deprecation of third party cookies from Google Chrome in 2024. First-party data in omnichannel marketing takes personalization to the next level, increasing a customer's lifetime value. What is Omnichannel Marketing? Omnichannel marketing seamlessly blends messaging and branding as customers move through online and offline touchpoints along the path to purchase. It puts consumers in the driver's seat, allowing them to choose how, when, and where to engage with your brand. An omnichannel marketing strategy prioritizes the customer experience through the effective use of a few key elements: Consistency in branding and messaging across every channel Personalized messaging and offers relevant to consumers interests and behaviors Content shaped by past interactions and the stage of the customer journey A well-planned omnichannel strategy lets you target customers at the right time with on-brand offers that increase your chance of a conversion. Omnichannel versus multichannel: What's the difference? Omnichannel and multichannel share similarities, but the differences are significant. Multichannel marketing gives consumers multiple options to engage with your brand, but the channels aren't seamlessly connected. The experience is optimized for each separate channel. On the other hand, omnichannel marketing recognizes that the customer journey spans multiple channels and seeks to create a consistent, personalized experience as the customer moves between them. The Coming “Cookie-geddon” Although Google's cookie deprecation timeline has changed a bit since they first announced the phaseout in 2020, the final demise of the third-party cookie is slated for 2024. The news didn't come as a surprise to anyone paying attention to the growing concerns of privacy advocates. Third-party cookies collect an enormous amount of personal data, usually without the individual's explicit consent. Data breaches and privacy violations caught the attention of legislators around the globe, resulting in the EU's GDPR and "cookie law." In the US, individual states passed their own versions of the cookie law in an attempt to promote transparency in data collection practices. A few tech CEOs also took a stand for privacy. Apple and Mozilla were among the first to give users the ability to block third-party tracking as early as 2012, with both companies disabling third-party cookies entirely by 2020. Google, the browser behemoth representing over 60% of Internet traffic, was the only holdout. But by 2020, it too announced it would end third-party cookies, albeit on its own, slightly elongated timeline. Now “Cookie-geddon” is almost upon us, and marketers are scrambling for solutions to replace the data cookies provided. What Does This Mean for Brands? Marketers have become addicted to the easy flow of third-party cookie data driving programmatic and digital advertising. It enabled personalization, targeting, and attribution to justify spend. But third-party cookies have their share of drawbacks: There's no transparency. The slightly underhanded way data is collected destroys the sense of trust between consumers and brands. Omnichannel marketing is a two-way street; consumers are willing to trust brands with their data in exchange for a more personalized experience as long as they feel confident their data is secure and only shared with consent. They're not people-based. Cookies are connected to devices, not people, so there's a lot of waste and duplicate impressions. They're not persistent. Cookies don't last forever, and the user can always delete them. Third-party data made it easy for brands to acquire new customers, lose them to churn, and reacquire them with aggressive retargeting. What it didn't do is help them build the trust and loyalty that drives long-term profits. Customer retention has always been key to profitability; invesp , a conversion rate optimization consultancy, showed that increasing retention by just 5% led to a 25% increase in profits. On the other hand, first-party data from past brand interactions and logged-in states give marketers the information they need to genuinely understand their customers and create highly relevant experiences throughout the customer lifecycle. Leveraging first-party data in omnichannel marketing levels up the personalization and relevancy of the content you serve your customers. Where retention spreads customer lifetime value over a longer timeframe, personalization increases the absolute lifetime value of the customer. Boston Consulting Group found that marketers who could deliver relevant experiences at multiple touchpoints decreased costs by 30% and increased revenue by 20%. title: Batch payments for Mexico contractors: a founder checklist
summary: How founders and finance teams can prepare recurring Mexico contractor payments with saved beneficiaries, approval rules, proof, and reconciliation.
body_text: If you pay the same Mexico contractors every week or every month, the payment flow should not depend on rebuilding a spreadsheet every time. Batch payments are useful because they turn recurring contractor payroll into an operating process: who gets paid, how much, in what currency, with what approval, and with what proof. What belongs in a contractor-payment batch A useful batch template should include: contractor name; legal or invoice reference; receiving bank details; MXN or USD payment instruction; recurring amount or variable amount field; approver; proof destination; accounting reference. The goal is not to make payroll complicated. The goal is to avoid improvising when everyone is waiting for money. Before you click approve Run a quick payroll check: Are all contractor bank details current? Are new contractors separated from recurring contractors? Is the FX rule clear for this pay cycle? Does someone know who receives payment proof? Can finance reconcile this payment next month without asking operations? Is there a backup approver if payroll happens outside normal hours? This checklist matters more as the team grows. Why payment status matters For contractors, silence creates anxiety. If the payment is moving but not yet visible, a status update or proof trail can reduce the number of follow-up messages. For the company, that visibility also helps separate a real payment issue from a normal processing window. title: Real-life lessons in work and money
summary: Through Junior Achievement programs, BOK Financial volunteers help students learn practical lessons about money, work and responsibility
body_text: KEY POINTS Hands-on programs like Junior Achievement help students see what’s possible and can influence their long-term goals and aspirations. Real-world lessons on budgeting, taxes, credit and everyday expenses help young people make smarter financial decisions later in life. A few hours spent with students can build confidence, broaden perspectives and inspire them to imagine a different future for themselves. All Daniel Agundiz expected going in was to have a fun time with his friends. But this, it turned out, was no ordinary fifth-grade field trip. Junior Achievement's Tulsa BizTown would pack a lot more meaning into the experience. "I remember how much I enjoyed helping people and feeling like I had a real responsibility," said Agundiz, whose pretend job for the day was at a Bank of Oklahoma working model. "It wasn't just playing anymore to me. I felt like I was part of something important." Looking back today, Agundiz, who grew up to become a real banker for Bank of Oklahoma, is more grateful than ever for the BizTown experience, which he credits with opening his eyes to what was possible. He plans to pay it back soon as a Junior Achievement volunteer. A nonprofit that helps young people learn about work readiness, entrepreneurship and financial literacy through hands-on programs, Junior Achievement has enjoyed a long and productive relationship with BOK Financial®. Over the years and across various markets, company employees have supported the organization as volunteers, board members and advocates. For many, it has become a practical way to help students get early exposure and build confidence around money and careers. Real-world wake-up calls Agundiz's experience is not unusual. For students who participate, Junior Achievement programs often open their eyes to the world of work, money and everyday decisions, while at the same time inspiring them to think more strategically. Monte Moore has seen it time and again over his 20-plus years volunteering with the organization. “It’s that 'a-ha' moment when you can see that light bulb go off in their heads,” Moore said. “Maybe it needs to be reinforced later, but you know they’re going to remember parts of it.” A process improvement consultant for BOK Financial, Moore has worked with various ages and grade levels through Junior Achievement. At Jenks East Elementary in Jenks, where he volunteers in the classroom, the lessons are kept very basic, he said. "At that age, nobody has any idea what they want to do, so it’s about just putting a thought in their mind to what kinds of jobs people can do in the community to make it better. It doesn’t matter what job you do. The point is to get involved and do things." From there, as students encounter other Junior Achievement offerings, the lessons grow more advanced. That's especially true in Finance Park, a program geared toward high school students where participants are assigned jobs, salaries and budgets. Moore, who volunteers with that program as well, said students usually begin the exercise feeling confident about their assigned income. “They get excited when they get their job. Then the taxes hit—and that always takes a little bit of wind out of their sails.” As students work through the cost of housing, food, transportation, insurance and utilities, it serves as a real-world wake-up call, he said. “They’re like, ‘Is that really how much this costs?’” Moore said. “We say, ‘Actually no, it’s probably a little low. It's probably higher.’” Volunteers may never know the full impact of those moments for any one student. However, for Moore, the chance that just one or two leave with something that sticks makes the effort worth it. Even if it's only that they'll be a little smarter with money. “I’ve seen it firsthand through my career: poor decisions early in life, especially with credit, can stick with you for your whole life," said Moore. "A little education and a little involvement to help prevent those poor decisions helps everybody. It helps the community.” Seeing a 'different tomorrow' For Thomas Hay, chief operating officer of consumer banking for BOK Financial, that impact is part of what has kept him connected to the organization for so long. A longtime Junior Achievement volunteer and advocate, Hay currently serves as chairman of its Tulsa Region Board. In addition to 15-plus years of board service, he's continued working directly with youths, both in the classroom and through a variety of Junior Achievement programs. His belief in the mission comes partly from his own experiences, he said. Hay did not participate in the program as a student. However, at an important point in his youth, three people came along separately and had a profound influence on him, he explained. “Through the impact and counsel of other people, I saw different pathways in my own life that changed my life,” Hay said. That's part of what he sees happening through Junior Achievement. Volunteers may only spend a few hours with students, but the encounters can still leave an impression. People who have been involved with Junior Achievement for decades often describe it as planting a seed, Hay continued. “You don’t always get to see the treetop,” he said. “On occasion, you do.” For Hay, Daniel Agundiz’s story feels like one of those occasions: an example of a student experience lasting far beyond the day itself. “The fact that Daniel remembers that, to me, is the most tangible value,” Hay said. “It feels especially cool that he’s got that story and he’s part of our family at the bank.” Still, Hay said, the larger goal is not to create future bankers. “We’re just trying to help young folks see a different tomorrow, whatever that might look like for them,” he said. Full circle Each year following a session, students who worked a day at Biztown's Bank of Oklahoma often write letters to the company. They talk about everything they learned—from how to make deposits and withdrawals, to using debit cards, to counting money and helping customers. One recent student, in thanking BOK Financial for his first work experience, summed it up this way: "Now I know why my parents are so tired." Agundiz was a student at Tulsa's Cooper Elementary School when BizTown provided his first taste of grown-up work. At the time, he didn't even realize he was working at a Bank of Oklahoma model, he said. He only learned that recently—when Erica Irvine, president of Junior Achievement of Oklahoma, came into his current branch on business. Agundiz saw her Junior Achievement button and was inspired to share his field trip story. Irvine filled in the missing detail. Upon learning where he'd been working, "in that moment, everything connected," Agundiz said. "I had started there without even realizing it, and somehow found my way back." Agundiz hopes soon to get his first experience volunteering for BizTown. He's tried before, he said, but "it fills up so quickly." When he does, though, he knows he'll enjoy being involved, helping create meaningful experiences for youths like the one that benefited him. "BizTown wasn't just about learning how the world works," he said. "It was about planting a seed in our little minds to become what was always meant for us." "There was something about that experience—the sense of purpose, the interaction with people, the responsibility: It quietly shaped how I saw my future." Learn more about volunteering opportunities with Junior Achievement in your market at jausa.ja.org .

title: Stop rewriting detection rules by hand: automatic Sentinel-to-Elastic migration is here
summary: Export your Sentinel rules, upload to Elastic, and get translated detections back. Scheduled, NRT, watchlists and severity mappings supported.
body_text: 29 July 2026 • Charles Davison Stop rewriting detection rules by hand: automatic Sentinel-to-Elastic migration is here Elastic's first automatic migration from a modern SIEM. Translate your Sentinel detection rules into Elastic Security without rebuilding them. 4 min read Detection Engineering , Product Updates Elastic automatically translates your Microsoft Sentinel detection rules into Elastic Security. Export your Scheduled and Near Real Time (NRT) analytics rules from Sentinel, upload them, and Elastic picks up the mapping and translation from there using an LLM you choose. Watchlists and severity mappings carry over. This is the first automatic migration path off a modern SIEM, available now in Tech Preview in 9.5, and it works across multiple cloud providers and regions so you can deploy closer to where your data lives. Which Microsoft Sentinel rule types can be migrated automatically? Automatic Migration focuses on the rules that carry your detection logic. In 9.5, it translates Scheduled and Near Real Time (NRT) analytics rules from Microsoft Sentinel, exported from your Sentinel workspace, and handles the translation for you. It uses the same mapping and translation as our existing rule migrations, now extended to Microsoft Sentinel. The following are supported: Integration identification with just rule export Support for the following rule types: Near-real-time (NRT) detection analytics rules Scheduled Analytic Rules Support for Watchlists to ES|QL Lookups Severity Mapping How to migrate Microsoft Sentinel detection rules to Elastic The migration runs in a few steps, from exporting your rules in Sentinel to reviewing the translated versions in Elastic. Once you've decided which rules and data to migrate, follow these steps: On the Security Launchpad, open Manage Automatic Migrations, select your AI provider, and expand Migrate your existing SIEM rules to Elastic. Select the drop-down on the top right for Microsoft Sentinel. Let Elastic guide you through exporting your rules from Sentinel and uploading them into Elastic Security. Elastic handles the finer details by scanning for watchlists and then prompts you to upload them when found. Once the rules are uploaded, you can view their status. Installed: Already added to Elastic SIEM. Click View to manage and enable it. Translated: Ready to install. This rule was mapped to an Elastic-authored rule, or translated by Automatic Import . Click Install to install it. Partially translated: Part of the query could not be translated. You may need to specify an index pattern for the rule query, upload missing files, or fix broken rule syntax. Not translated: None of the original query could be translated. Failed: Translation failed. Refer to the error for details. For more information, refer to the technical documentation . After clicking View Rules, you will have the ability to edit and install rules. Should you migrate rules first or data first? One of the first decisions in a migration is sequencing: data or rules first. Elastic supports both paths, so you can start wherever makes sense for your team. Path When to use What happens Rules first You do not know exactly which data sources to prioritise before moving any logs. Translate your Sentinel rules first. Elastic identifies which integrations those rules need, so you can plan data onboarding around what your detections actually require. Data first Your log sources are already being onboarded, or you want detections to work the moment they're installed. Onboarding data beforehand improves the translation quality. Onboard your log sources into Elastic, then migrate your Sentinel rules to match. Rules can be installed and enabled immediately against data that's already flowing. Custom data You have proprietary or non-standard log sources that don't map to a prebuilt Elastic integration. Use Automatic Import to ingest custom data sources in minutes, then migrate or write rules against them. By identifying exactly which integrations are needed before moving a single log, teams can build a precise, risk-aware roadmap for their migration project. This transparency eliminates the guesswork and helps ensure that critical visibility gaps are addressed long before you fully decommission your environment. What happens after your Sentinel rules are running in Elastic Once your rules are running in Elastic, Workflows lets you build automation around them. The moment a rule fires, a workflow can kick off multi-step remediation, enrichment, and notification automatically. And building these automations in Agent Builder lowers the barrier, so you can create a workflow in natural language. How Elastic AI fits into a Sentinel-to-Elastic migration Elastic Security brings generative AI into the SOC with retrieval augmented generation (RAG) and open agentic frameworks. Automatic Migration joins the lineup of Elastic Security’s AI features, helping SOC teams strengthen defenses across the IT environment: Automatic Migration for Detection Rules complements Elastic’s deep library of prebuilt rules to broaden detection use case coverage. Automatic Import extends visibility and powers detection rules by onboarding custom data sources in minutes. Agent Skills assist in the response process and less time context switching. Elastic’s SIEM and XDR solution helps analysts detect earlier and respond faster. Try automatic detection rule migration Migrating a SIEM has always meant rebuilding your detection rules by hand, and that cost is what keeps teams on a platform long after they've decided to leave. Automatic Migration simplifies that process, providing mapping to existing Elastic rules and helping to translate the rest. Your watchlists and severity levels carry over as well, and you move on your own terms, with your data and your tooling under your control. For further details check out our documentation . Try it free , or get in touch . Have feedback? Tell us what you think in the Elastic Community Slack channel or on the Elastic Security forum . title: ¿Cuánto cobra un contador por una declaración de renta?
summary: Si eres asalariado, sin inversiones ni propiedades adicionales, el precio suele empezar en $150.000. Si tienes varias fuentes de ingreso, inversiones, propiedades o activos en el exterior, el valor puede superar fácilmente el millón de pesos.
body_text: En Colombia, un contador cobra entre $150.000 y $3.500.000 de pesos por elaborar una declaración de renta, dependiendo de qué tan compleja sea tu situación tributaria. Si eres asalariado, sin inversiones ni propiedades adicionales, el precio suele empezar en $150.000. Si tienes varias fuentes de ingreso, inversiones, propiedades o activos en el exterior, el valor puede superar fácilmente el millón de pesos. Más abajo encontrarás una tabla con los rangos exactos para 2026, los factores que disparan el precio y cómo evitar pagar de más. Tabla de precios 2026: cuánto cobra un contador según tu tipo de declarante No existe una tarifa única porque la DIAN no regula los honorarios de los contadores independientes; cada profesional fija su precio según el tiempo que le tome tu caso. Con base en las tarifas reportadas por gremios contables y firmas de asesoría en 2026, este es el panorama general: Tipo de declarante Nivel de complejidad Rango de precio 2026 (COP) Asalariado con un solo empleador, sin inversiones ni propiedades Simple $150.000 – $400.000 Independiente con varios contratos o ingresos por honorarios Media $400.000 – $700.000 Con vivienda, vehículo, CDTs o inversiones en acciones/fondos Media-alta $700.000 – $1.200.000 Con ingresos del exterior, herencias o varias propiedades Compleja $1.200.000 – $2.000.000 Casos especiales: corrección de declaraciones anteriores, requerimientos de la DIAN o representación en un proceso de fiscalización Muy compleja $2.000.000 – $3.500.000 Nota: estos son promedios de mercado, no tarifas fijas. En ciudades como Bogotá, Medellín o Cali los honorarios tienden a ser más altos que en municipios pequeños, y los precios suben considerablemente en las últimas semanas del calendario tributario, cuando la demanda se dispara. Qué factores hacen que un contador cobre más o menos El precio final de tu declaración depende de una combinación de variables. Estas son las que más pesan: Complejidad de tu situación financiera. Entre más fuentes de ingreso, inversiones, propiedades o pasivos tengas, más tiempo le toma al contador revisar soportes y clasificar cada partida. Volumen y calidad de tus documentos. Si llegas con la información desordenada o incompleta, el contador debe invertir tiempo extra en organizarla, y eso se traduce en un cobro adicional. Experiencia y especialización del profesional. Un contador con maestría en impuestos o con experiencia específica en planeación tributaria suele cobrar más, pero también puede encontrar deducciones que compensan el costo. Ubicación geográfica. Las tarifas en las grandes ciudades suelen ser más altas por el costo de vida y la demanda del servicio. Momento del año en que contratas el servicio. Contratar con anticipación (junio o julio) casi siempre sale más barato que hacerlo en la última semana antes de tu vencimiento. Servicios adicionales. Si además necesitas asesoría para reducir el impuesto a pagar, corregir una declaración anterior o representación ante la DIAN, el valor se cobra aparte. Contador independiente, firma contable o plataforma digital: ¿qué te conviene? Antes de comparar precios, vale la pena entender que no todas las opciones para declarar renta son iguales. Estas son las alternativas más comunes en el mercado colombiano: Opción Precio típico Ventaja principal Cuándo elegirla Contador independiente $150.000 – $1.200.000+ Atención personalizada y asesoría a la medida Casos con inversiones, propiedades o ingresos variables Firma contable o de auditoría $500.000 – $3.500.000+ Respaldo institucional y garantía formal Empresas, altos patrimonios o casos con litigios fiscales Plataforma digital de autoservicio $0 – $250.000 Rapidez y bajo costo Declaraciones sencillas, un solo empleador Contador apoyado en herramientas de inteligencia artificial Similar a un contador tradicional, con tiempos de entrega más cortos Cruce automático de soportes, menor margen de error humano Independientes y empresas que buscan agilidad sin perder el acompañamiento profesional En los últimos años, cada vez más contadores y firmas en Colombia están adoptando copilotos contables con inteligencia artificial para automatizar la causación de facturas, la conciliación bancaria y la clasificación tributaria. Esto no reemplaza al contador, pero sí reduce el tiempo operativo que antes se cobraba dentro de los honorarios, lo que en la práctica se traduce en procesos más rápidos y, en muchos casos, tarifas más competitivas para el cliente final. Documentos que debes entregarle a tu contador El precio también depende de qué tan preparado llegues. Antes de tu cita, reúne: Certificado de ingresos y retenciones (si eres asalariado) o certificados de honorarios (si eres independiente). Extractos bancarios de todas tus cuentas del año gravable. Certificados de inversiones: CDTs, fondos de inversión, acciones o criptoactivos. Soportes de activos: escrituras de vivienda, tarjetas de propiedad de vehículos, avalúos. Soportes de pasivos: extractos de créditos hipotecarios, de vehículo o préstamos con particulares. Recibos de pago del impuesto predial y del impuesto de vehículos. Planilla de aportes a seguridad social (PILA) si eres independiente. Declaración de renta del año anterior, como referencia para el contador. Certificados de ingresos del exterior, si aplican. Cuanto más completa y ordenada llegue esta información, menos tiempo tendrá que dedicar el contador a organizarla, y eso puede bajar tu factura final. Cómo evitar pagar de más (y no caer en estafas) Pide una cotización por escrito antes de entregar tus documentos. Un contador serio te dará un rango de precio después de conocer tu caso, no un número improvisado por teléfono. Verifica la tarjeta profesional del contador en el registro de la Junta Central de Contadores. Esto te protege de personas que se hacen pasar por contadores sin estar habilitadas para firmar declaraciones. Desconfía de precios extremadamente bajos cuando tu declaración es compleja: puede significar que no van a revisar a fondo tus soportes, lo que te expone a errores y sanciones posteriores. No dejes tu declaración para la última semana. La demanda dispara los precios y aumenta el riesgo de que la plataforma Muisca de la DIAN se congestione. Compara al menos dos o tres cotizaciones si tu caso es complejo, especialmente si involucra inversiones, propiedades o ingresos del exterior. Qué pasa si no declaras a tiempo (y por qué contratar a un contador puede salir más barato) Para el año gravable 2025, la DIAN estableció que las personas naturales deben presentar su declaración de renta entre el 12 de agosto y el 26 de octubre de 2026, según los dos últimos dígitos de su cédula. Se estima que cerca de siete millones de personas naturales tendrán esta obligación en 2026. Estás obligado a declarar si en 2025 tuviste, entre otros casos, consumos con tarjeta de crédito, compras o consignaciones bancarias superiores a 1.400 UVT (unos $69.719.000). Para 2026, cada UVT equivale a $52.374. Si no presentas la declaración a tiempo, la sanción por extemporaneidad equivale al 5% del impuesto a cargo por cada mes o fracción de mes de retraso, y la sanción mínima para 2026 es de 10 UVT, equivalente a unos $524.000, incluso si no tenías impuesto a pagar. En muchos casos, el costo de un contador termina siendo más bajo que el de una sanción por errores o por no declarar. Preguntas frecuentes ¿Vale la pena pagar un contador si mi declaración es sencilla? Si solo tienes un empleador y no tienes inversiones ni propiedades, puedes usar plataformas digitales de bajo costo o incluso la plataforma gratuita Muisca de la DIAN. Un contador se justifica cuando quieres asegurarte de no cometer errores o cuando buscas identificar deducciones que reduzcan el impuesto a pagar. ¿Los honorarios de un contador tienen IVA? Sí. Los servicios contables prestados por personas naturales responsables de IVA generan el impuesto sobre el valor del servicio, así que confirma si el precio cotizado lo incluye o no. ¿Puedo negociar el precio con mi contador? Sí, especialmente si contratas con anticipación o si le llevas la información completamente organizada. Muchos contadores ajustan su tarifa según el tiempo real que les tome el caso. ¿Qué pasa si mi contador comete un error en mi declaración? La responsabilidad de lo declarado sigue siendo tuya ante la DIAN, aunque puedes reclamarle al contador por negligencia. Por eso es clave verificar su tarjeta profesional y, si es posible, contratar servicios que ofrezcan algún tipo de garantía o acompañamiento en caso de una revisión posterior.

title: Lear Wins 2025 Automotive News PACE Award for its Innovative Zone Control Module
body_text: SOUTHFIELD, Michigan, April 16 - Lear Corporation (NYSE: LEA), a global automotive technology leader in Seating and E-Systems, has won a 2025 Automotive News PACE Award for its groundbreaking Zone Control Module featuring Algorithmic Circuit Protection. Lear's Zone ControlModule (ZCM) facilitates the OEM shift to zonal architectures, where vehicle electronics are organized by physical zones instead of traditional domain-based configurations. Central to this innovation is its advanced Algorithmic Circuit Protection, a groundbreaking approach that redefines power management. The ZCM revolutionizes circuit protection by replacing traditional hardware fuses with a cutting-edge, software-defined model. "Winning the 2025 Automotive News PACE Award is an honor that underscores Lear's dedication to innovation," said Nick Roelli, Senior Vice President and President of Lear E-Systems. “This technology represents a significant step forward, combining exceptional performance with cost efficiency. It simplifies vehicle systems while providing real, tangible benefits to our customers.” This adaptive algorithm delivers tailored circuit protection while providing flexibility for automakers to add more features and functions in their vehicles. By shifting to this innovative technology, the ZCM enhances customization capabilities and establishes new opportunities for advanced vehicle designs. The Automotive News PACE Awards, recognized worldwide as the premier standard for innovation in the automotive industry, have celebrated groundbreaking advancements by suppliers for more than 30 years. In the last decade, Lear has earned multiple PACE Awards for its innovative technologies, including Configure+, Configure+ with zonal safety technology, and the Battery Disconnect Unit.

title: Additions to Executive Team Reinforce Vertiv Growth Agenda
summary: Vertiv, formerly Emerson Network Power, today announced multiple additions to its executive team as it accelerates into its second year as a private company. The new appointments fortify the business for anticipated growth in 2018 as Vertiv continues to reposition itself in its key markets and organize around its core tenets: customer focus, innovation, employee development, and speed.
body_text: Columbus, Ohio [Feb. 20, 2018] – Vertiv, formerly Emerson Network Power, today announced multiple additions to its executive team as it accelerates into its second year as a private company. The new appointments fortify the business for anticipated growth in 2018 as Vertiv continues to reposition itself in its key markets and organize around its core tenets: customer focus, innovation, employee development, and speed. Heading into its second year of independence after separating from former parent company Emerson, Vertiv and the leadership team are focused on enhancing customer relationships, streamlining information-sharing internally, and shortening innovation cycles across the company. The leadership team also continues to evaluate all aspects of the business, including the Vertiv portfolio of products and services, the markets it serves, and its global footprint and operations. The full executive team reporting to CEO Rob Johnson now includes: Giordano Albertazzi , president, Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA). Albertazzi has spent nearly 20 years in ascending roles across the Emerson Network Power and Vertiv organizations, at various times assuming responsibility for plant management as well as services and sales for EMEA. Frank Bibens, president, global services. Bibens has been in this role since 2011. He joined the organization in 2006 following a 28-year career with GE and is responsible for the Vertiv services team. Andrew Cole, chief organizational design and human resources officer. Over the past 20 years, Cole has led organizational development programs, corporate talent strategy, leadership development, and change management for multiple global companies and holds all of those responsibilities with Vertiv. David Fallon , chief financial officer. Fallon brings more than 25 years of experience in financial management with global companies to his current role managing the Vertiv financial portfolio. He most recently served as chief financial officer at Clarcor, Inc. Victor Fetter, chief digital officer. Fetter has more than 25 years of experience in using technology to strategically grow global businesses, and at Vertiv is responsible for continuing the transformation of the customer’s digital experience as well as the use of technology for operational excellence. Colin Flannery, worldwide general counsel. A 20-year veteran of corporate law, Flannery most recently served as worldwide general counsel of Sensus, a multinational smart grid technology corporation. He leads the Vertiv legal team. Jason Forcier, executive vice president, infrastructure and solutions. Forcier is responsible for large infrastructure products and solutions. He joined Vertiv in 2017 after eight years with A123 Systems, the last four as CEO. John Hewitt, president, the Americas. Hewitt is responsible for Vertiv activities in the U.S., Canada and Latin America, including Mexico. Before joining Vertiv, Hewitt held various leadership roles with technology companies in the U.S. and abroad. Pat Johnson , executive vice president, integrated rack systems. Johnson, a veteran of 20 years in the data center business, joined Vertiv in 2017 and today oversees the integrated rack systems portfolio. Most recently, he served as senior vice president of strategic initiatives for Artesyn Embedded Technologies. Stephen Liang , president, Asia-Pacific. Liang started with Emerson in 1994 and has been in his current role since 2009. He leads Vertiv activities in Greater China, Greater India and Asia. Tarek Maguid, chief operations officer. Maguid is responsible for global operations, supply chain, and shared services. He most recently held the same position with BWAY Corporation. Gary Niederpruem, chief strategy and development officer. Niederpruem, a 20-year veteran of the organization, is responsible for leading the Vertiv strategy, corporate development and marketing functions. Angelica Smallwood, chief of staff. Smallwood is responsible for coordinating and executing enterprise-wide initiatives. She most recently worked on mergers and acquisitions at Nationwide Insurance. “In our first year as Vertiv, we have strengthened and streamlined our internal systems and processes, eliminated waste, and sharpened our focus on our customers,” said Vertiv Chief Executive Officer Rob Johnson. “We will build on our progress by investing in employee development and bold, innovative additions to our portfolio, all with an eye toward the ever-changing needs of our customers.” Vertiv and the leadership team kicked off 2018 with a pair of significant acquisitions. Vertiv announced the purchase of Energy Labs, a global manufacturer of air handling solutions, and Geist, a global manufacturer of Rack Power Distribution Units, in January. “The executive team we have put together over the past 12 months has been instrumental in the acquisitions and ongoing integration of Energy Labs and Geist,” Johnson said. “They bring exceptional experience and enthusiasm to everything we do, and have embraced our culture of collaboration, innovation and transparency.” For more information, visit www.VertivCo.com . About Vertiv Vertiv designs, builds and services critical infrastructure that enables vital applications for data centers, communication networks and commercial and industrial facilities. Formerly Emerson Network Power, Vertiv supports today’s growing mobile and cloud computing markets with a portfolio of power, thermal and infrastructure management solutions including the Chloride®, Liebert®, NetSure™ and Trellis ™ brands. Sales in fiscal 2016 were $4.4 billion. For more information, visit VertivCo.com . CONTACT Vince McMorrow T +614 383 1622 E Vince.McMorrow@Fahlgren.com
